reason: The wording is Murdoch's and the essay is right, but the page is wrong, and it is wrong in the one field the verifier claims to have corrected by opening the book. I downloaded the PDF the evidence names, eganphilosophy.com Murdoch-The-Sovereignty-of-Good-Over-Other-Concepts.pdf, and extracted its text. Its copyright page reads First published 1970 by Routledge and Kegan Paul, First published in Routledge Classics 2001, First published in Routledge Great Minds 2014, so it is the edition the source names. The sentence appears exactly as proposed: It is a task to come to see the world as it is. It sits in the paragraph that ends And to this the whole activity of our consciousness is relevant, three sentences after Of course virtue is good habit and dutiful action. I then mapped every printed page number in the file by reading the running head of each sheet. The essay's numbered pages run 76, 77, 78 and so on in unbroken sequence to 101, on PDF sheets 4 through 29, so PDF sheet n carries printed page n plus 72. The sentence is on PDF sheet 17, whose running head reads the sovereignty of good over other concepts 89. Printed page 90 is the next sheet, which opens difficult task of virtue look easier and more attractive and does not contain the sentence at all. So the citation should read p. 89, not p. 90. Two smaller errors ride with it. The evidence says the page numbers run 76 to 101 across the essay; the essay in fact opens on the unnumbered chapter page 75, PDF sheet 3, headed 3 THE SOVEREIGNTY OF GOOD OVER OTHER CONCEPTS. And the locator says in the paragraph beginning Of course virtue is good habit and dutiful action, which is not where that paragraph begins. Everything else is sound and the line can ship on the corrected citation: shipped.js returns no exact match and no near match, iris murdoch stands at 2 of 3 for the year from February and March so this is her last, she is not banned, the work is first published 1970, the tag Philosophy is the form of the work, the source line is 107 characters with the corrected page, leads with her name, carries no em dash, and the quotation ends in a full stop with no straight double quote. I refute it because a page number that names a page the sentence is not on is a confident false citation, and the note stakes the correction on having opened that page.
